question: I'm on the free plan, uh, can a company take money by direct debit without asking me?
expected_answer: No, a company can only collect by direct debit after you've authorised a direct debit instruction; you can cancel it any time, and the direct debit guarantee gives you an immediate refund of any payment taken in error.
answer_aliases: no, you must authorise it first

key_facts: a direct debit needs your authorisation first
the direct debit guarantee refunds payments taken in error

question: Okay, and how much would that one actually cost me each month, roughly speaking?
expected_answer: Plus costs £4.99 a month, with a 6-month minimum term.

history.content: I'm thinking about upgrading from the free plan.
Sure, the Plus plan adds a few extras for travel and cash withdrawals.

key_facts: £4.99 a month
6-month minimum term

question: If I upgrade to Plus and don't like it, can I cancel it next month?
expected_answer: Plus has a 6-month minimum term: you can cancel early, but the remaining monthly fees up to the end of the 6 months are charged in one go.

key_facts: 6-month minimum term
remaining monthly fees up to the end of the 6 months are charged in one go
meta.common_prior: Yes, paid account plans are monthly subscriptions you can cancel any time and simply stop paying.

question: Why did the shop make me put my PIN in when contactless usually works fine?
expected_answer: For security, card rules require a chip-and-PIN check after a run of consecutive contactless payments or a certain cumulative amount, to confirm it's really you; entering your PIN resets the count.
answer_aliases: chip and PIN after several contactless payments

key_facts: security check after several contactless payments in a row
entering the PIN resets the count

question: Why was I charged a fee for taking cash out of a normal cash machine?
expected_answer: Cash withdrawals are only fee-free up to £250 in any rolling 30 days on Standard (£600 on Plus); above that a 2% fee applies, even at free-to-use UK machines.

key_facts: first £250 of cash withdrawals in any rolling 30 days is fee-free
2% fee applies
including free-to-use machines in the UK
meta.common_prior: UK cash machine withdrawals are free from your bank; any fee would come from a pay-to-use machine's operator.

question: Can I avoid extra fees abroad by paying in pounds instead of the local currency?
expected_answer: No, pay in the local currency; choosing pounds lets the shop or cash machine provider convert it for you (dynamic currency conversion), usually at a worse exchange rate.

key_facts: choose the local currency
paying in pounds uses the merchant's worse conversion rate

question: I'm on the free plan, are there any fees for using my card abroad?
expected_answer: Some: on Standard, card payments abroad are fee-free up to £1,000 per calendar month, then a 1% fee applies, and cash withdrawals abroad count towards your £250 fee-free cash allowance.

key_facts: fee-free up to £1,000 per calendar month
1% fee
£250 per rolling 30 days on Standard
meta.plausible_wrong_answer: Yes, card payments abroad are completely fee-free; you only pay the exchange rate.

question: What's the difference on cash withdrawals abroad if I move up to the Plus plan?
expected_answer: Plus gives you £600 of fee-free cash withdrawals in any rolling 30 days, at home or abroad, instead of £250 on Standard; above that it's 2%.

key_facts: first £600 of cash withdrawals in any rolling 30 days is fee-free
£250 per rolling 30 days on Standard

question: Uh, what does the AER bit actually mean on that rate?
expected_answer: AER stands for annual equivalent rate: it shows what you'd earn over a year with interest compounded, so you can compare savings accounts that pay interest at different frequencies.

history.content: I'm looking at opening the Easy Access Saver.
Sure, I can tell you how it works and what you'd earn on it.

key_facts: annual equivalent rate
lets you compare accounts that pay interest at different frequencies

question: Can I take money out of my Easy Access Saver whenever I want?
expected_answer: You can withdraw instantly, but only 3 withdrawals per calendar year keep the full rate; from the 4th withdrawal the rate drops to 1.00% AER for the rest of that calendar year.

key_facts: only 3 withdrawals per calendar year keep the full rate
rate drops to 1.00% AER for the rest of that calendar year
meta.plausible_wrong_answer: Yes, easy access means unlimited withdrawals at any time with no effect on the rate.

question: Um, what rate are you paying on the Easy Access Saver at the moment?
expected_answer: It's 3.10% AER variable, with interest calculated daily and paid monthly.

key_facts: 3.10% AER variable
paid monthly

question: If Confirmation of Payee says the name doesn't match, could I lose my money by paying?
expected_answer: You can still choose to pay, but yes: if the account isn't who you think, the money can be hard to get back, so check the exact name with the payee first, since a mismatch can be a typo, a business name or a scam.

key_facts: the payment can still be sent but may be hard to recover
check with the payee before sending

question: Uh, why hasn't my payment to someone I just added as a payee arrived yet?
expected_answer: If it was over £1,000, the first payment to a new payee is held for up to 24 hours for fraud checks before it's sent; smaller payments go immediately.

key_facts: first payment over £1,000 to a new payee is held for up to 24 hours
meta.common_prior: Bank transfers by Faster Payments arrive within seconds or at most two hours, so it should already be there.

question: Is there a limit on how big a single bank transfer from my account can be?
expected_answer: Yes, a single payment can be up to £10,000, and you can send up to £25,000 per day in total.

key_facts: single payment can be up to £10,000
£25,000 per day

question: Can a chargeback get my money back even when the shop refuses to refund me?
expected_answer: Yes, that's what it's for: after you dispute the payment, your card provider can reverse it through the card network without the shop's agreement, although the shop can challenge it with evidence.

key_facts: a chargeback is reversed through the card network
it does not need the merchant's agreement

question: Why won't the app let me dispute a card payment from six weeks ago?
expected_answer: Disputes must be raised within 30 days from the transaction date, and ones raised later aren't accepted, so a six-week-old payment is outside the window.

key_facts: within 30 days from the transaction date
disputes raised later are not accepted
meta.common_prior: Card disputes can usually be raised up to about 120 days after the transaction, so six weeks should still be fine and it is probably an app glitch.

question: So, um, what does a temporary credit mean once I've disputed a payment?
expected_answer: It means that if your evidence supports the dispute, the disputed amount is credited within 10 working days while the chargeback runs; a final decision follows within 45 days, and the credit is reversed with 7 days' notice if the merchant wins.

key_facts: temporary credit for the disputed amount within 10 working days
final decision is made within 45 days

question: Okay, a pending payment just disappeared, so how much of that money actually left my account?
expected_answer: None of it: a pending payment is only an authorisation hold, and if the merchant cancels it or never collects it, the hold expires and the money is released, so it never actually left your account.

key_facts: a pending payment is an authorisation hold
the hold is released if the merchant doesn't collect

question: Why's the hotel deposit still blocked on my card, like, when does it drop off?
expected_answer: Hotel holds can last up to 31 days, and we can't release them early unless the hotel confirms in writing that it has cancelled the authorisation, after which we release it within 1 working day.

key_facts: Hotel, car hire and cruise holds can last up to 31 days
release the hold within 1 working day

question: If I find my card after reporting it lost, can I still use it?
expected_answer: No, reporting a card lost or stolen cancels it permanently for security, so it can't be reactivated even if you find it; you'll use the replacement card instead.

key_facts: the card is cancelled permanently
it can't be reactivated

question: How does getting a new card work if I've lost mine, and is it free?
expected_answer: Report it lost in the app, which cancels the card, and it isn't free on Standard: a replacement for a lost or stolen card costs £5; on Plus, one lost or stolen replacement every 12 months is free.
answer_aliases: free once a year on Plus

key_facts: a replacement for a lost or stolen card costs £5
one lost or stolen replacement every 12 months is free
meta.common_prior: No, banks replace lost or stolen debit cards free of charge.

question: How quickly do replacement cards usually arrive, is there a faster option?
expected_answer: Standard delivery takes 3 to 5 working days and is free; express next-working-day delivery costs £12 if you order before 4 pm, Monday to Friday.

key_facts: standard delivery takes 3 to 5 working days
next working day for £12 if you order before 4 pm

question: Is the EAR on an overdraft the same as an APR, or not quite?
expected_answer: Not quite: EAR is the effective annual rate of interest on an overdraft, including the effect of compounding but only covering interest; APR also includes fees and is the figure used for loans and credit cards.

key_facts: EAR is the effective annual interest rate
APR includes fees as well as interest

question: If my balance goes a little bit below zero, do you charge me anything?
expected_answer: No fee: there's no unarranged overdraft, so such payments are normally declined free of charge and an accidental negative balance carries no fee or interest; with an arranged overdraft, the first £25 is interest-free, then 29.9% EAR applies.

key_facts: does not offer unarranged overdrafts
no fee or interest is charged
first £25 of overdraft use is interest-free
meta.plausible_wrong_answer: Yes, going overdrawn without an arranged overdraft means unarranged overdraft interest or a fee.

question: Is there a legal reason I need a selfie and photo ID to open an account?
expected_answer: Yes: banks are legally required under anti-money-laundering and know-your-customer rules to verify who you are; the selfie confirms the photo ID belongs to the person applying, which stops impersonation and fraud.

key_facts: identity checks are legally required
the selfie matches you to the ID

question: Okay, so how long have I got before something happens to my account?
expected_answer: You have 30 days from the request to complete reverification in the app; after that, card payments and outgoing transfers are paused until it's done, though incoming payments still arrive.

history.content: I got a notification in the app saying I need to verify my ID again.
Yes, that's a routine check we run on accounts from time to time.

key_facts: 30 days from the request
card payments and outgoing transfers are paused

question: Okay, so they want me to move my money into a safe account today, should I?
expected_answer: No, that's a scam: a genuine bank will never ask you to move money to a 'safe account', so don't transfer anything, hang up and report it.
answer_aliases: never move money to a safe account

history.content: I just got a call from someone saying they're from your fraud team.
Thanks for checking with us. Can you tell me what they asked you to do?

key_facts: it's a scam
a bank will never ask you to move money to a safe account

question: How does reporting fraud to you work if it happens in the middle of the night?
expected_answer: Call the fraud line on 0808 157 0436, which is open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week (+44 20 7946 0436 from abroad), and you can freeze your card in the app straight away.

key_facts: open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week

question: Do I need my sort code as well as my account number to get paid?
expected_answer: Yes: for UK bank transfers the payer needs both, because the six-digit sort code identifies your bank and the eight-digit account number identifies your account.

key_facts: both the sort code and account number are needed
the six-digit sort code identifies the bank

question: How many hours is your phone line actually open on a Saturday?
expected_answer: The phone line is open 9 am to 5 pm on Saturdays; in-app chat is available 24 hours a day.

key_facts: 9 am to 5 pm on Saturdays
In-app chat is available 24 hours a day
